findings.evidence: ## When to use — When a run, a review or an execution step calls an external AI CLI and acts on the result.
findings.fix: The description already carries WHEN. Delete this H2 (record the removal) or replace it with one decision the description cannot show, such as which stop is an owner stop versus a hard-tier wait.

findings.evidence: ## References lists the same two files the opening paragraph already gates, plus the runner template path.
findings.fix: Keep the runner-template path (it is not in the opening). Drop the two links that lines 21-24 already load, and record that removal.

findings.evidence: Process pattern is right, but sections 2, 4 and 6 pack several decision trees into single paragraphs (run lock, argv-file, idle watchdog, blocked-until) instead of the phased checkpoints the pattern uses.
findings.fix: Split each of those paragraphs into a short decision list at the step that uses it (lock held / stale / unreadable; formula missing / argv-file; idle off / review / execute), and leave the tables as the checkpoint.

findings.evidence: ## Pitfalls is a bullet list, not a Gotchas section, and several items state the fact without the non-obvious why (Copilot's prompt on argv; two timeouts; atomic rewrites keep the file mode).
findings.fix: Rename the section Gotchas and add the reason an expert learned: Copilot's prompt is visible in the process table because the runner moves it onto argv; a hand replace of a config or state file drops the mode an atomic rewrite keeps.

findings.evidence: references/subprocess-quota-policy.md is gated ('read it when you configure the runner's retry table'), but launch-and-wait.md is mandatory before every first launch and the policy file is also pulled in from sections 2, 5 and 6.
findings.fix: Keep the policy file for the configure/[runner.retry] branch only. Point the launch, session-pin and hard-tier steps at the SKILL.md section that already states the rule, and load launch-and-wait.md only for the host that is actually launching.

findings.evidence: Section 5 offers two equal callers for a partial lane (GSD abort versus a self-managed one-shot resume) and section 6 offers two equal wake forms, with the choice stated but easy to take as a menu.
findings.fix: State one default per branch: under GSD, abort and stop; outside GSD, one resume then stop. For the wake, CronCreate only where that tool is callable, otherwise the print-and-stop handoff, never both.

findings.evidence: 8 should-trigger and 8 should-not-trigger queries; the rubric asks for about 20, with 8-10 of each, and the negatives miss a near-miss such as reading a runner log without launching or answering a stop.
findings.fix: Add two should-trigger queries (a locked bare 75; a partial execute resume) and two near-miss should-not-trigger queries (explain a cross-ai.mjs log the user already pasted, with no launch or stop to answer; edit the runner template itself).

findings.evidence: Ten cases have realistic prompts and verifiable assertions, but eight of ten have files: [] and two assertions only restate the skill text.
findings.fix: Add lane.err fixtures for the locked bare-75, partial task_uncovered and retry_after_s cases, and assert the decision read from that file (no wait scheduled; one resume naming Task 2; wait exactly retry_after_s).

findings.evidence: The run-lock paragraph names three refusals (live child group, another host, unreadable after 2s) but the exit-code table only says a bare 75 is an owner stop, so a caller cannot tell which refusal to report.
findings.fix: Add one row under the lock: child group still running, other host, or unreadable record each end locked with a bare 75; report the printed line and do not clear the record or re-invoke.

findings.evidence: pi, cursor, codex and copilot are each marked unverified and then repeat the same foreground command already shown for Claude Code.
findings.fix: Keep one 'unverified, no background primitive: use the foreground block' line and delete the four copied command blocks; the Claude Code block stays the only pattern.
